QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_38

question.text: Of the seven Social Stock Exchanges set up globally before India, how many are still functioning as per Chapter 2, and in which countries?

answer.text: Five — Brazil, South Africa, Canada, Singapore and Jamaica.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.1, 'three out of the seven Social Stock Exchanges that were set up still survive and function. They are based in Canada, Singapore and Jamaica.' Brazil (2003), South Africa (2006), Portugal (2009) and UK (2013) — of the original seven — have ceased or substantially wound down. The Trap: Option A over-counts. Option C is simply wrong. Option D under-counts by excluding Canada and Jamaica. Cross-Exam Context: XII (SMF) references global exchange failures as a teaching example. XV (RA) touches Singapore IIX for impact-bond valuation. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When citing global precedent in your SIR (Social Impact Report), stick to Canada's SVC (FPE-focused), Singapore's IIX (equities + Women's Livelihood Bonds) and Jamaica — using defunct exchanges (Brazil's BVSA or UK's SSE) as benchmarks dates your report and signals weak research to SEBI reviewers.
